label: ledger-final
brand: the Ledger fixture's own identity: a warm-paper fintech dashboard in the Mercury/Anthropic lane — ivory paper, one clay accent, serif numbers-as-headlines, small tool-like radii, light-first

defects: Header row is truncated: '80 Oct 2026 - In $47.4k...' cuts off at the right viewport edge, breaking the calm grid.
Chart x-axis labels are illegible: 'SCRUB DAYS' text and tick labels are too light and small to meet WCAG contrast ratios.
Status tags like 'pending' and 'failed' rely on color and low-contrast text, making them difficult to distinguish for colorblind users or in low-light conditions.
The 'Where it went' table header 'STATUS :' and 'ACCOUNT' columns are visually cramped against the right edge, creating tension in the otherwise generous layout.
The 'DISCLOSURES' section is a monolithic gray block that disrupts the paper-white rhythm and buries the 'not a bank' disclaimer in low-contrast text.
improvements: Fix header row truncation to ensure full data visibility on standard desktop viewports.
Increase chart axis text size and contrast to meet WCAG AA standards for legibility.
Add text labels to status tags to ensure accessibility for all users.

critiques.label: The company's money, in plain figures
defects: Horizontal clipping on the top-right card, causing the 'vs prior quarter' text to run off the edge without padding or scroll.
Inconsistent baseline alignment: the subtext on the Runway card is not vertically aligned with the '4 accounts' subtext on the Cash Position card.
The chart x-axis timeline is visually disconnected from the '30 Oct 2026' legend metadata, creating a spatial gap between data and context.
The scrubber handle (orange dot) is too far right, visually unbalanced and not centered relative to the active 90-day data range.
Type scale inconsistency: 'Annualized Revenue' is slightly larger than 'Runway', breaking the uniform rhythm of the four top cards.
improvements: Increase horizontal padding on the right-side card to prevent text clipping and overflow.
Align all card footers to a single, consistent baseline grid for better visual cohesion.
Add left-aligned time labels under the x-axis to anchor the chart timeline properly.

critiques.label: In, out, and the net between
defects: The large dead vertical space between the chart card’s legend (net/inflow/outflow) and the 'TRANSACTIONS' eyebrow breaks the rhythm and wastes ~120px of real estate.
The 'SCRUB DAYS' slider control is visually orphaned at the bottom-left of the chart card, disconnected from the data it manipulates and lacking any visible value readout or tick marks.
Header metadata ('30 Oct 2026 · in $47.4k...') is right-aligned but its baseline doesn't align with the H2 'In, out...' left baseline, creating a subtle eye-skip.
Table column 'AMOUNT' and 'STATUS' headers use a small, light-weight sans-serif that is barely legible against the ivory background at 100% zoom, failing WCAG for secondary text.
The 'settled' status pill has a low-contrast light-green background with dark-green text; the contrast ratio is likely below 4.5:1 for the small font size.
improvements: Tighten vertical spacing: reduce gap between chart card and 'Where it went' section by 40%.
Align slider control to right or center it under chart; add visible value label next to handle.
Increase table header font weight to 500 and darken color to #444 for WCAG AA compliance.

critiques.label: Where it went
defects: The 'seeds fixture' label in the top right is truncated and collides with the viewport edge, destroying the clean fintech dashboard identity.
Status pills are inconsistent: 'pending' uses a beige background while 'failed' uses a jarring red, breaking the 'one clay accent' palette rule.
The eyebrow text 'TRANSACTIONS - THIS MONTH' is nearly invisible and lacks adequate spacing from the H1 'Where it went', muddying the visual hierarchy.
The date column uses a monospaced font while the rest of the table uses a sans-serif, creating a subtle typographic dissonance.
improvements: Increase contrast on status pills to meet WCAG AA standards for legibility.
Unify the typeface for dates and amounts into a single clean sans-serif.
Add generous padding to the top-right metadata to prevent viewport truncation.

critiques.label: Four buckets, one position
defects: The 'ACCOUNTS' section label (00:29:00) is too faint; it lacks contrast against the ivory background, failing WCAG for non-essential text.
The 'The fine print' disclaimer section (00:29:46) is visually detached from the rest of the ledger; the grey box feels like a separate footer rather than part of the main data flow.

The sub-captions under the card titles (e.g., 'Day-to-day spend, cards, AP' at 00:28:34) are slightly cramped against the title above, reducing the breathing room characteristic of the 'calm density' baseline.
The account identifiers at the bottom of the cards (e.g., '9417 •••• 3382' at 00:28:44) are in a very small font that risks legibility on lower-DPI desktops.
The transition from the transaction table to the 'Four buckets' cards feels abrupt; there is no subtle divider or whitespace rhythm change to signal the shift in content type.
improvements: Increase 'ACCOUNTS' label font weight or darken color for WCAG legibility.
Integrate disclaimer into main flow with a subtle top border instead of a grey box.
Increase vertical spacing between card titles and sub-captions to 4px.

critiques.label: The fine print, on purpose
defects: The 'DISCLOSURES' and 'ACCOUNTS' overline labels are severely low-contrast, using faint gray that likely fails WCAG AA for normal text.
Vertical spacing rhythm is broken: a massive, empty gap separates the four account cards from the disclosure block, making the layout feel fragmented.
The footer is isolated by a large void of empty background space, leaving the composition feeling top-heavy and unbalanced.
The legal copy in the disclosure section, while legible, has a slightly loose line height that hurts scanning efficiency compared to the tighter text above.
improvements: Darken the 'ACCOUNTS' and 'DISCLOSURES' overline labels to improve contrast and readability
Tighten vertical spacing between the account cards and disclosure block for unity
Balance footer margin to prevent excessive whitespace at the bottom of the viewport

defects: Typography: The serif numerals in the 'CASH POSITION' card ($3,733,800) lack sufficient font-weight to justify their massive scale against the tiny 10px labels, causing them to look airy and weak.
Alignment: The primary header 'The company's money, in plain figures' is horizontally misaligned with the 'CASH POSITION' card directly below it, breaking the left margin.
Color: The status pills use high-saturation greens and bright reds that break the 'warm-paper' muted brand lane, making them look like default UI controls rather than a calm fintech system.

Visual Hierarchy: The chart subtitle ('In, out, and the net between') is visually smaller than the meta-text ('TRANSACTIONS - THIS MONTH') on the transaction table, breaking the top-down reading order.
Layout: The 'SCROLL DAYS' slider sits in a massive empty white space, failing to utilize the horizontal room to improve the density of the chart section.
improvements: Increase font weight of primary serif numerals to 400 or 500.
Align section headers to the left edge of the data cards.
Mutify status pill colors to match the paper/clay palette.
Scale up section titles in the table and chart areas.
Move the days slider closer to the chart for better grouping.

defects: The clay accent color used in the 'Open an account' button, chart lines, and '12.7%' pill is too light against the warm paper background, failing WCAG AA contrast for small text.
The '12 rows' and 'seeded fixture' subtext under the 'Where it went' header has extremely low contrast and is nearly illegible.
The cash flow chart is rendered with very faint, washed-out lines that blend into the background, destroying the data's legibility and breaking the 'serif numbers' boldness of the rest of the UI.

The transaction table's right-aligned amounts (AMOUNT column) appear visually truncated or crammed against the right edge, lacking a clear, consistent right-alignment padding gutter for the currency values.
The monospace font used for card numbers (e.g., '9417 •••• 3382') and secondary data looks too small and low-contrast, straining the eye on a mobile viewport.
improvements: Darken clay accent to a rich terracotta for WCAG AA contrast compliance across all UI elements.
Increase chart line opacity to 80% and add subtle background gridlines to restore data legibility.
Apply consistent 24px right-padding to the transaction table's amount column to prevent edge cramping.

critiques.label: The company's money, in plain figures
defects: Top header 'OVERVIEW AS OF 30 OCT 2026' is cut off mid-glyph at the viewport edge, breaking the eyebrow and causing a broken first impression.
Card inner padding and label-to-number spacing varies slightly; 'RUNWAY' card uses more vertical space than 'CASH POSITION' despite smaller content, disrupting rhythm.

Delta chips (green/red) use inconsistent visual weight against the card background; the red 42.5% chip's border and fill create slightly higher contrast than the green chip, reading as uneven severity.
Serif figures ($3,733,800 vs $107,211 vs 17 mo) use the same scale, so the '17 mo' feels visually weaker than the currency figures despite being a key KPI.
Alignment of the small supporting text ('4 accounts · seeded fixture Q4 FY26') sits flush left but optically drifts from the number above due to the leading space after the bullet.
improvements: Fix clipped eyebrow; add top padding or move header inside the card grid so nothing is cut at the viewport edge.
Normalize all KPI cards to identical min-height, padding, and label-to-figure gap for a strict vertical rhythm.
Equalize delta chip visual weight; match border, fill, and type size between green and red chips so severity reads symmetrically.

critiques.label: In, out, and the net between
defects: Chart is visually broken: dense red spike lines obscure the intended 'in/out/net' distinction, rendering the data nearly unreadable.
Typography contrast is weak: the 'In, out, and the net between' headline is small and muted relative to the 'Where it went' headline below, inverting visual hierarchy.
The 'SCRUB DAYS' slider is vertically misaligned with the 'Y-axis clamps...' caption text, creating an awkward visual gap.
The transaction table header 'AMOU' is cut off, and the negative value '-$4,' is incomplete, indicating a critical layout overflow error.
The 'SCRUB DAYS' control lacks clear affordance; the track is faint and the thumb is disconnected from its purpose.
improvements: Redraw chart with distinct line weights and colors for in/out/net to ensure data legibility.
Increase headline font size and weight for 'In, out...' to establish clear primary hierarchy.
Fix table overflow to display full 'AMOUNT' header and complete transaction values.

critiques.label: Where it went
defects: Mobile truncation of 'MERCHANT' and 'AMOUNT' headers due to lack of overflow handling or abbreviations.
Right-aligned column amounts (e.g., '–$4', '–$9,') are visibly clipped, breaking data legibility.
Date column 'DATE ▼' has inconsistent vertical alignment with merchant names, causing a visual jitter.
Green text (e.g., '$48,') on the light paper background fails WCAG contrast for smaller type.
Row dividers lack sufficient padding-top/bottom, making the list feel cramped and dense.
improvements: Replace 'MERCHANT' with 'NAME' and 'AMOUNT' with '$' to prevent mobile truncation.
Expand right padding and font sizing to prevent numerical data clipping on mobile.
Increase row vertical padding to 16px to improve calm density and readability.

critiques.label: Four buckets, one position
defects: Cards float without a unifying container; the group reads as four disconnected tiles rather than one ledger section.
Horizontal padding inside each card is inconsistent with the section header's left edge, breaking the intended vertical alignment grid.
Monospaced account suffix (e.g., '9417 •••• 3382') is visually noisy and weakly related to the amount, cluttering the 'headline number' moment.
'Four buckets, one position' headline is heavy relative to the thin card typography, making the section header feel more important than the data it introduces.
Vertical gap between the last card and the next section starts tighter than the rhythm established above, breaking spacing consistency.
improvements: Wrap cards in a single bordered panel; inset each card 16px with internal padding 24px.
Snap all left edges to one 24px grid; align account suffix to amount baseline.
Shrink monospace suffix to 11px, 60% opacity; add 'Account' label for clarity.

critiques.label: The fine print, on purpose
defects: Tax card: '9417 .... 2296' is rendered in a tiny 8-9px sans-serif, creating a weak, noisy footer that fails to match the serif numeric hierarchy of $366,800.
Disclosures container: The grey background box creates a heavy visual wall that competes with the 'Tax' card above, breaking the calm density and warm-paper continuity.
Typography: The body text within 'The fine print' uses a monospace or narrow sans-serif that clashes with the elegant serif headline, creating a typographic disconnect.
Footer: 'Not a bank . Not advice' is visually underwhelming, using dots as separators which feels like a code placeholder rather than a designed element.
Spacing: The vertical gap between the 'Tax' card and the 'Disclosures' section is inconsistent with the gap between the 'Disclosures' box and the footer.
improvements: Upgrade the 9417 account number to the brand serif typeface for numeric consistency and elegance.
Remove the grey background box from disclosures, using whitespace and a subtle hairline for separation.
Replace the dot separators in the footer with subtle vertical rules or increased tracking.
